claim: On host nativestack-5975wx-20260925 on 2026-09-26, Prometheus 3.15.0 was qualified against the running 3.14.0 and then switched into production. The release asset prometheus-3.15.0.linux-amd64.tar.gz (111,651,578 bytes) hashed to sha256 2a542df32eac02ee17b9d844fb2aa1de00dafa5476579ba8a3ba862e9d572ea0, equal to the GitHub API asset digest and to the release's sha256sums.txt (sha256sum --check --strict: OK); the repository's unchanged observability/backends/install.py, run from a scratch copy beside a one-entry pins.json, verified it again and extracted it into a new tools/ecosystem-prometheus-3.15.0 prefix that is byte-identical to the archive, and prometheus and promtool report 3.15.0 at revision 5241a27fe3c6983549fccc32f6e65917408c63cd, the v3.15.0 tag commit. promtool 3.14.0 and 3.15.0 both passed check config and check rules (14 rules) on the live files. On copies of the live TSDB (115,828,843 bytes, 11 blocks plus WAL) with the live config minus `alerting`, 3.14.0 and 3.15.0 ran side by side on scratch loopback ports: each was ready in about 1 s, scraped the same seven live targets (all up), loaded 2 rule groups and 14 rules with health ok, reloaded on SIGHUP, logged no ERROR line and returned the same 7-series, 511-sample `up` query_range over the six hours before the copy (sha256 22d1cb61... in both). After 3.15.0 stopped, 3.14.0 opened the TSDB 3.15.0 had written, was ready in about 1 s, returned the same history and read the 5 self-scrape samples 3.15.0 had written. tests/test_observability_backends_alerts.py, now reading its promtool and amtool paths from observability/backends/pins.json, ran 18 tests OK with promtool 3.15.0. The unit observability/backends/configure.py renders with the 3.15.0 pin and the host's saved port overrides differs from the live unit only in the ExecStart prefix; that unit was installed, passed `systemd-analyze --user verify`, and ecosystem-prometheus.service was restarted at 2026-09-26T04:56:49Z. /-/ready answered 0.86 s after the restart call; buildinfo reads 3.15.0 at 5241a27f; the seven targets are up; 14 rules evaluate with health ok; the six-hour `up` history before the switch (7 series, 511 samples) hashes the same before and after; and the journal since the restart has no ERROR line. bin/prometheus and bin/promtool name the 3.15.0 prefix. At a read-back at 05:17:53Z the unit had NRestarts 0, the two alerts that fired before the switch (for endpoints this host does not run) were firing again with their original Alertmanager startsAt, and ntfy had no new message since 04:55Z. The cutover ran switch.py, which logged its verify, daemon-reload and restart exit codes and its post-switch comparisons without making the link change depend on them; in this run every one of them passed before the links moved (cutover/switch.json). Its replacement switch_gated.py moves the links only after every gate passes and otherwise restores the previous unit. On a scratch unit with the live unit's restart settings (gate-rehearsal/results.json, 2026-09-26T10:03:07Z to 2026-09-26T10:08:11Z) it switched 3.14.0 to 3.15.0 and back, refused a wrong running version without changing anything, and restored 3.14.0 without moving the links when daemon-reload failed, when daemon-reload silently did not reload, when the new server could not start (after its crash loop hit the start limit), and when the restarted server still reported 3.14.0.
limitations: Reviewed once: a review round of the refresh coordinator (Claude Opus and GPT-6 Astra reviewers) reported that switch.py repointed the bin links whatever its verify, daemon-reload, restart and post-switch checks said; this revision repairs it (switch_gated.py and its failure-injection rehearsal gate-rehearsal/). The repair itself has not been re-reviewed, and the qualification and this receipt still come from one worker family (Claude Opus 5.5).

switch_gated.py has not switched the production unit. It was rehearsed only on a scratch unit (fresh TSDB, one self-scrape target, two rules, five-second scrape and evaluation intervals, a 20 s settle instead of 45 s, a six-hour history holding one sample at the 300 s step), with faults injected by a systemctl shim and two fake prefixes that answer --version as 3.15.0; the production cutover ran switch.py.

The landscape ledger does not move here: catalogs/landscape/foundation.json keeps the observation-inference winner pin prometheus 3.14.0 from the sealed 2026-09-22 layer-verdict packets. Receipts at 3.15.0 stay unbound until a new verdict wave re-records the layer.

Linux x86_64 only, one host. The pin lives in observability/backends/pins.json (linux-amd64); adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json and adoption/pins-macos-arm64.json have no Prometheus entry. Nothing here is macOS evidence.

The rehearsal ran each arm for about 75 s plus a 20 s rollback start on a TSDB copied with cp while the live server wrote. No head block was compacted in that window, so a rollback after 3.15.0 has written its own compacted blocks is untested; the float chunk encoding stays XOR by default at v3.15.0 (stage/source-checks.txt), which is the source-level basis for expecting such blocks to stay readable.

Release notes were read from the release body; upstream tests were not run on this host. The PromQL changes and fixes can move rule results in edge cases; the host's 14 rules kept health ok and the same firing set.
No signature was verified: the release publishes checksums only, and the v3.15.0 tag is PGP-signed but GitHub reports it unverified (bad_email) and the signature was not checked locally.

The switch restarted the service: scrapes pause for about a second, and rules with `for` re-enter pending before their restored firing state; the read-back found the pre-switch firing set restored without a new notification.

Not aligned here: catalogs/us-equities/agents-operations.json and .md still name Prometheus v3.14.0 (trading-catalog alignment, as #310 did for ai-memory); observability/README.md describes the 2026-09-19 acceptance at 3.14.0; docs/stack.md is a 2026-09-19 snapshot.

data.rollback: switch_gated.py with the two versions and prefixes swapped, revision d7598b7141418fa35be2b5ec5d0fefb634199610 and an expected unit rendered with the 3.14.0 pin (the direction rehearsed as G2 on the scratch unit). By hand: put the 3.14.0 prefix back in ExecStart, systemctl --user daemon-reload, reset-failed and restart ecosystem-prometheus.service, check /-/ready and buildinfo 3.14.0, then relink bin/prometheus and bin/promtool to tools/ecosystem-prometheus-3.14.0 (kept)
data.overturn_when: 3.15.0 misbehaves on this host's rules or TSDB (for example a compaction or WAL error), a 3.15.x patch fixes a defect that matters here, or a verdict wave selects another metric store
data.switch_procedure: switch_gated.py: preflight that changes nothing on failure (exit 1); back up and install the expected unit; gates on verify, daemon-reload, the loaded unit (NeedDaemonReload=no, ExecStart names the new prefix), restart, /-/ready and a new MainPID, then after a settle period version, revision, ExecStart, NRestarts 0, targets, rules, the six-hour history and the journal; the bin links move last. Any failure after the install restores the backup unit (reset-failed before its restart) and exits 2, or 3 if the restore fails too.
